newsitem.title: CHINA: China grain harvest seen at record high.
newsitem.headline: China grain harvest seen at record high.

text.p: China's grain harvest could reach nearly 480 million metric tons this year, beating 1995's record output by 15 million tons, the China Daily Business Weekly said Sunday.
A rise in the state purchasing price of cereals earlier this year had encouraged farmers to grow more grains, the newspaper quoted economists of the State Statistic Bureau as saying.
The increase in the area of land under grain would boost production despite devastating floods that struck vast swathes of cropland in July and August, it said.
While Ministry of Agriculture officials remained cautious about China's agricultural situation, statistics bureau economists were making no secret of their faith in a bumper harvest, it said.
China's summer grain harvest was more than 110 million tons this year, up three percent from last year, while early rice output rose 4.2 percent to 44 million tons, it said.

China has been importing 11 million tons of wheat a year to make up for domestic shortages, while a rising demand for meat had caused shortages in corn and soybean, widely used as feed for livestock, it said.
Meat output was expected to hit 60 million tons in 1996, a 15 percent rise compared with last year, it said.
China reaped a record 465 million tons of grain in 1995 and has set a target of 465 million tonnes for 1996.
